items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Because I’m interested in medicine, from the standpoint of Hippocrates and Paracelsus.

ctx.x: So you’re not just totally a music-oriented person.

Never was. No. I’ve always had a literary side to me. I got the only A in my Creative Writing class in seven years. The professor, Dr. Milton Marks, wrote the textbook that was used in Harvard, Yale, Princeton, all the universities. And he hadn’t given an A in seven years. And he gave me one. And I got the only A in my speech class in four years. And I was a history minor and I got all A’s in that. So I’ve always been interested in several other things — like I say, everything else. I was interested in…

medicine, he never operated on anybody, and treated nervous disorders with higher mathematics. Because numbers quiet the nervous system. Because numbers are what everything is made of. There’s a book in the Bible called “Numbers.” So if you get interested in the numerical aspect of anything, your nerves quiet down. This is medicine.
